facts.condition: For a finite Marton construction over two channel uses to exceed the duplicated optimum of the single-use randomized schedule, its induced distribution on the four paired inputs must be an interior point of that simplex; every boundary face is excluded.
Such an improving two-use construction must remain uniformly separated from each input-simplex face, with distinct certified margins for the two symmetry classes of paired inputs.

assumptions: The accepted result is scoped to finite-auxiliary Marton laws for exactly two channel uses.
The comparison benchmark is the independently duplicated optimum of the single-use randomized schedule specified by the accepted claim.
No unrestricted block-code converse or exact sum-capacity conclusion is inferred from this support condition.
